episode_summary: Episode 277 (October 2019) opens with a roundtable on Bitcoin as money (store of value, medium of exchange, unit of account), mining centralization, and Tim Cook's criticism of Facebook's Libra. The main interview is with Nicolas Dorier, Bitcoin Core contributor and CEO of BTCPay Server, covering why BTCPay exists, its Lightning and SegWit support, hosting and funding, refunds, and his views on Taproot, block size and confidential transactions.

cards.claim: In October 2019 the host said cryptocurrencies had problems with the medium of exchange and unit of account roles of money, except for the Bitcoin Cash community.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: cryptocurrencies having problems satisfying the medium of exchange and unit of account aspects of money.

cards.claim: In October 2019 a roundtable guest argued that a currency only has value when there is a tradable scarcity, which digital assets can provide.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: You can only have value when there's a tradable scarcity.

cards.claim: In October 2019 a roundtable guest said using Bitcoin to buy coffee was a waste because the cost per transaction was too high.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: Using Bitcoin to buy coffee probably isn't a good idea. It's a waste.

cards.claim: In October 2019 the host predicted proof-of-work mining would centralize into a few big players, with the largest holding around 21 to 22 percent of the network.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: Mining is going to move to a point where there will be some big bosses in the game

cards.claim: In October 2019 Nicolas Dorier said you often hear that something decentralized cannot be built on top of something centralized, while Bitcoin itself is decentralized.
cards.speaker: Nicolas Dorier
cards.quote: you often hear that you cannot build something decentralized on top of something centralized.

cards.claim: In October 2019 Nicolas Dorier said building a business directly on Bitcoin was complicated, so developers relied on intermediaries such as BitPay and BlockCypher.
cards.speaker: Nicolas Dorier
cards.quote: building your own business on top of bitcoin was pretty complicated stuff

cards.claim: Nicolas Dorier said he created BTCPay Server so developers could build apps on Bitcoin without deep technical skills, Bitcoin Core knowledge, or middlemen.
cards.speaker: Nicolas Dorier
cards.quote: so that's when I created BTC Pay basically so that people can build apps on top of Bitcoin without deep technical skills that require Bitcoin Core

cards.claim: Nicolas Dorier said he was a freelance Microsoft certified trainer before discovering Bitcoin.
cards.speaker: Nicolas Dorier
cards.quote: before Bitcoin I was a Microsoft certified trainer

cards.claim: Nicolas Dorier said he began looking into Bitcoin after Mt. Gox, wondering why it was not dead yet.
cards.speaker: Nicolas Dorier
cards.quote: it was after MT Gox III I start looking around Bitcoin because I was wondering why it's not dead yet

cards.claim: In October 2019 Nicolas Dorier said the Bitcoin base layer was fine and he was very bullish on it.
cards.speaker: Nicolas Dorier
cards.quote: I think the base layer is fine. So I'm very bullish.

cards.claim: Nicolas Dorier said BTCPay was likely the first payment processor to accept Lightning, around March 2018.
cards.speaker: Nicolas Dorier
cards.quote: who could say that we are the first uh payment processor to accept lining i i think it's us

cards.claim: Nicolas Dorier said he implemented SegWit in his NBitcoin library while SegWit was still being developed.
cards.speaker: Nicolas Dorier
cards.quote: when segwit was being developed i at the same time i was implementing it at nbitcoin level

cards.claim: Nicolas Dorier explained that BTCPay lets merchants price invoices from chosen exchanges, with premiums and averaging rules, such as 50% Coinbase and 50% Kraken.
cards.speaker: Nicolas Dorier
cards.quote: you can say okay I want to let the price come 50% from Coinbase 50% from Kraken and I take the average of it

cards.claim: Nicolas Dorier said BTCPay was evolving from a merchant tool into a server for individuals, including crowdfunding features he did not expect.
cards.speaker: Nicolas Dorier
cards.quote: it becomes more like a server for individuals, not only for merchants

cards.claim: Nicolas Dorier said BTCPay can act as a wallet using a hardware wallet to sign or export PSBTs.
cards.speaker: Nicolas Dorier
cards.quote: you can really use it as a as a as a wallet and use your hardware wallet to sign

cards.claim: Nicolas Dorier admitted that BTCPay's refund process was not very good, with no clear rule on whether refunds are paid in dollars or bitcoin.
cards.speaker: Nicolas Dorier
cards.quote: like our refund process is not very good

cards.claim: In October 2019 Nicolas Dorier said LunaNode was the cloud host BTCPay recommended for merchants who were not technical.
cards.speaker: Nicolas Dorier
cards.quote: So the Luna Node deployment doesn't require any technical skill.

cards.claim: In October 2019 Nicolas Dorier said concentrating BTCPay hosting on LunaNode was a risk, and he was talking to a new host provider.
cards.speaker: Nicolas Dorier
cards.quote: if everybody starts using LunaNode and something happens, then it will be a big drama.

cards.claim: In October 2019 Nicolas Dorier said about 99 percent of BTCPay deployments used only Bitcoin, because running a full node made other chains costly.
cards.speaker: Nicolas Dorier
cards.quote: frankly speaking as far as BTC base concern 99 percent of deployments just at Bitcoin

cards.claim: In October 2019 Nicolas Dorier said BTCPay had no plan to make money and had set up a foundation to receive donations.
cards.speaker: Nicolas Dorier
cards.quote: there is no plan to make money so we built a foundation

cards.claim: In October 2019 Nicolas Dorier said Square Crypto gave the BTCPay project a grant of 100,000 through its new foundation.
cards.speaker: Nicolas Dorier
cards.quote: square crypto provide provided us a grant of one uh 100 000 uh to the project

cards.claim: In October 2019 Nicolas Dorier estimated there were around five thousand BTCPay deployments, with no reliable way to confirm the number.
cards.speaker: Nicolas Dorier
cards.quote: I don't know it's like a number of top of my head but maybe five thousand but I have

cards.claim: In October 2019 Nicolas Dorier said Lightning payments would always be cheap for merchants, while Bitcoin on-chain was still cheap at the time.
cards.speaker: Nicolas Dorier
cards.quote: the only way to ensure it's the case if the merchant is using lightning network and lightning network it will be cheap always

cards.claim: In October 2019 Nicolas Dorier said accepting Bitcoin is easier for global merchants than card payments, which bring processing fees, chargebacks and rejections.
cards.speaker: Nicolas Dorier
cards.quote: it's very time sink on the other hand when you accept bitcoin like you know it always works

cards.claim: In October 2019 Nicolas Dorier said Bitcoin's real strength was accepting money from anyone anywhere without conditions, not low fees.
cards.speaker: Nicolas Dorier
cards.quote: so I think it's where bitcoin really shines is not in the fees it's in the fact that you can accept money from whoever you want

cards.claim: In October 2019 Nicolas Dorier said he only used services that accepted Bitcoin, after failing to pay with foreign cards in Japan and with Microsoft Azure.
cards.speaker: Nicolas Dorier
cards.quote: right now when I'm using a service on Internet I only use service that accept Bitcoin

cards.claim: In October 2019 Nicolas Dorier said BTCPay wanted to build a tax tool where a merchant could load local tax policy and transactions to calculate what to declare.
cards.speaker: Nicolas Dorier
cards.quote: I think another thing I want to provide at one point is a tool where you can say

cards.claim: In October 2019 Nicolas Dorier said his short-term Bitcoin priority was Taproot and Schnorr signatures, which he expected to enable many new things.
cards.speaker: Nicolas Dorier
cards.quote: what I what I want in the short term is really a taproot and snore that will allow lots of new things happening

cards.claim: In October 2019 the host said Bitcoin should increase the base layer block size a little, as a fee-reducing move.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: we increase the block size just just a little bit

cards.claim: In October 2019 Nicolas Dorier said the 2017 SegWit-era block time increase was immoral, because it made it harder to run a full node and protect Bitcoin.
cards.speaker: Nicolas Dorier
cards.quote: I was okay with the block times increase like that we had during segway but by retrospective I think it was it was immoral

cards.claim: In October 2019 Nicolas Dorier said confidential transactions would not come to Bitcoin in his lifetime.
cards.speaker: Nicolas Dorier
cards.quote: I don't see confidential transaction coming anywhere near Bitcoin in my lifetime on my side.

cards.claim: In October 2019 Nicolas Dorier said Bitcoin as a design is done, and that fungibility debates would not change it.
cards.speaker: Nicolas Dorier
cards.quote: as a design, Bitcoin is done, like people do what they want.

cards.claim: Asked to describe Bitcoin in ten words or less, Nicolas Dorier answered with freedom.
cards.speaker: Nicolas Dorier
cards.quote: I have only one actually that come in my mind which is freedom

cards.claim: In October 2019 Tim Cook said a cryptocurrency should stay in the hands of countries and called Facebook's Libra a power grab.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: I really think that a cryptocurrency that a currency should stay in the hands of countries.

cards.claim: In October 2019 the host said the Federal Reserve is a gaggle of private banks, so the US system already runs on privately owned institutions.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: The Federal Reserve is a gaggle of private banks. So we're literally using that system right now.

cards.claim: In October 2019 the host argued Facebook's Libra was better than banks but not good enough, because the governance group was not broad enough.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: Now, I would argue that Libra is better than banks,

cards.claim: In October 2019 the host said Bitcoin and Ethereum were the two kings of crypto, and that would not change unless something new came along with a use case.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: The two Kings of the castle right now are Bitcoin and Ethereum.

title: The Bitcoin Podcast #277 - Nicolas Dorier - BTCPay Server
